Subscribe now

-
- Israeli soldiers and settlers have been besieging three Palestinian families in their homes in the village of Qusra in the occupied West Bank since August 9. Photo on August 14, 2026 by Issam Rimawi/Anadolu via Getty Images.RAMALLAH, Occupied West Bank—For the 12th consecutive day, three Palestinian families, comprising 10 people, including two young children, have been trapped inside their homes in the occupied West Bank, besieged and terrorized by dozens of armed Israelis—both settlers and soldiers. The family members have been stuck in separate homes, unable to shelter together or attend to their basic needs, with food supplies running dangerously low and without access to cooking gas or a fridge.
While the siege on the three families has garnered international media attention and statements of condemnation, the attack is not the first of its kind, but rather a more prominent example of a growing tactic by Israeli settlers and soldiers working in tandem to dispossess Palestinians from their homes in the West Bank. The attacks are increasingly focused on Palestinian communities in Area B, a designation under the Oslo Accords where the Palestinian Authority is nominally in charge of civil administration while Israel retains security control.
The latest Israeli siege targeted a small cluster of Palestinian homes that sit atop a hill on the edge of the village of Qusra, in the southern part of the Nablus governorate in the northern West Bank.
On the morning of August 9, armed settlers blocked off the only road leading to the homes and erected a colonial outpost directly in front of the door of one of the houses. They began pelting the homes with rocks and trying to break inside on a regular basis.
Israeli occupation forces eventually arrived on the scene and removed the outpost, but the settlers were able to erect it again, a pattern that repeated several times. And despite brief clashes with Israeli forces, the settlers were allowed to remain and continued to roam the area freely.
The settlers also cut off access to water and electricity and for more than a week prevented anyone—including emergency workers or ambulances—from reaching the families trapped inside. Qusra municipality employees were eventually allowed to repair the water and electricity lines after being initially assaulted by settlers and detained by Israeli forces.
Israeli troops have also exacerbated the situation by occupying two of the Palestinian homes they claim to be protecting.
On August 14, soldiers forced Yousef and Ruqayya Hassan and their two daughters, four-year-old Kinda and two-year-old Hour, from their home and into their neighbor’s unfinished villa, which belongs to Loui Abu Ridi, a U.S. citizen. Still unfinished, Abu Ridi’s home lacked basic furniture, including beds.
“It feels like there was a death in the family. We’re all distressed, angry and in a state of sadness,” Ruqayya told Drop Site in a phone interview.
Israeli troops occupied another neighboring home that was still under construction and belonged to Abou Ridi’s brother, Raed. The soldiers also erected a tent around twelve meters away, according to the mayor of Qusra, Abdelatheem Wadi.
“It’s the armed settlers on one hand and the military on the other,” Wadi told Drop Site, characterizing the trapped families in Qusra as being under a “double siege.”
Meanwhile, Ruqayya’s daughters fell ill and started exhibiting flu-like symptoms, with a fluctuating fever and a heavy cough. On the afternoon of August 12, Ruqayya and both her daughters were allowed to temporarily evacuate from the area in an ambulance to a medical clinic for treatment. It was when she and her daughters returned to the besieged area two days later that they found Israeli soldiers occupying their home and were ordered to move into Abu Ridi’s.
Another home belongs to Ruqayya’s brother-in-law, Rizq Hassan, who is trapped inside along with his 61-year-old mother and sister. The Israeli military has separated the families and prevented them from seeing each other.
“My daughters keep asking me why their teta (grandmother) is right next door and yet they can’t be with her. They are very distressed. How on earth can I explain what’s happening to them?” Ruqayya, adding that the psychological and physical toll was already visible in her eldest daughter. “Kinda has started urinating involuntarily. Even during the day, when she’s awake, she wets herself,” she said.

## “Complete Siege”
The fact that Abou Ridi, a U.S. citizen, was the owner of one of the homes may have helped spark statements of condemnation, including from staunchly pro-Israel U.S. officials like Ambassador Mike Huckabee, who called the settlers “Israeli terrorists” and their actions “criminal,” though Washington did nothing to intervene. Abou Ridi traveled from Ohio back to Palestine on August 17 to join his brother Qusai and his nephew who were staying in his home along with Ruqayya, her husband, and two daughters.
Those staying in Abou Ridi’s home eventually received supplies of food, water, and medicine from a UNICEF team on August 17, as well as personal care supplies for Ruqayya and her daughters. Those in Rizq Hassan’s home, which is under less of a spotlight, were not as fortunate.
“My brother-in-law’s home is under complete siege. They’re not allowed to leave the front door. They don’t have gas, or a fridge—they’re living on bread and a few canned items,” said Ruqayya. “No one is talking about them.”
Wadi, the mayor, said they are being abused by soldiers. “The aid brought in by UNICEF to Rizq Hassan’s home was left by soldiers in the yard for 24 hours in the sun, before the family was allowed to receive it, and half of it was already ruined,” Wadi told Drop Site. “There is media attention only on Loui’s home.”
The military and settler siege expanded beyond the three homes on August 13, when hundreds of Israeli occupation soldiers stormed Qusra and imposed a curfew across the entire village. Soldiers took over at least eight homes and forced their families out. According to Wadi, they severely vandalized the houses, damaging furniture and belongings.
The soldiers withdrew days later from the eight homes and the rest of the village, but they declared the area of the three besieged homes a closed military zone. Wadi estimates at least 50 to 60 soldiers remain stationed in and around the area of the besieged homes.
While the military claimed this order would be over by Tuesday evening, it remains in place, according to the residents.

-
- Israeli security forces and settlers gather outside the besieged Palestinian houses in the village of Qusra, in the occupied West Bank on August 17, 2026. Photo by Jaafar ASHTIYEH / AFP via Getty Images.

## “The New Reality”
Palestinians in the occupied West Bank have been coming under a steadily escalating assault for the past three years. Israeli settler attacks backed by Israeli soldiers and the state have fully or partially displaced 107 communities since January 2023, alongside unprecedented settlement expansion, according to a new report by Human Rights Watch. The Israeli military expelled another 32,000 Palestinians from their homes in the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams camps in January 2025.
The besieged families in Qusra have been under assault since January, when settlers first took over a nearby building that was under-construction and began launching daily attacks on the residents.
Their homes lie in Area B of the occupied West Bank. While settler attacks and the forcible transfer of Palestinians in recent years have largely targeted villages and Bedouin communities in Area C—which comprises roughly 60% of the West Bank and includes almost all the agricultural land—Israeli settler violence and theft of land is now increasingly spreading into Palestinian communities located in Area B.
Last month, a Palestinian family of eight living in the nearby village of Jalud, were forced from their home after a similar 10-day settler and soldier siege. The concentrated attack began three months prior, when settlers erected a colonial outpost near the Al-Tubassi family and began targeting them on a daily basis.
“During the final month, the settlers occupied a house under construction on the road to the Al-Tubassi family home, and in the last 10 days they cut off the water, electricity and no one could reach them any more,” Bashar Qaryouti, a medic and activist in the area, told Drop Site. “In the last four days the family had no food, nothing left, and on the final day they were held at gunpoint by the settlers and forced to leave.”
In a statement last week, the UN Human Rights Office condemned the attacks on Qusra. “These criminal actions by the settlers, supported or acquiesced to by Israel, the Occupying Power, are making life unbearable for these Palestinian families, and are clearly aimed at forcing them to leave their homes and land. Time is running out for these three families before they are forcibly displaced,” the UN Human Rights Office said. “The International Court of Justice is clear that all Israeli settlements are illegal and that Israel is obligated to cease all settlement activities, evacuate all settlers, including those terrorizing Qusra and Jalud, and bring to an end its unlawful presence in the West Bank.”
Analysts also warn that the recurrence of the siege tactic in Qusra is ominous and points to a wider pattern unfolding across the occupied West Bank.
“It began with Bedouin Palestinians in the remote areas, then it moved to the small villages at the edges of the governorates, and now they are in large villages, with the active participation of the military, which also supplies the weapons and trains them,” Ramallah-based political analyst Nihad Abu Ghosh told Drop Site.
In addition to the tens of thousands of Palestinians forcibly displaced over the past three years in the West Bank, over 1,000 Palestinians have also been killed, nearly a quarter of them children.
“These are fascist, Jewish-Zionist militias who are carrying out pogroms and killings in the occupied West Bank,” continued Abu Ghosh. “Both the government and the settlers are in a race against time. They consider the few remaining months or days of this government’s tenure to be an exceptional opportunity to change the reality on the ground. That is why they are intensifying their attacks until they reach a point where, in their assessment, it will be difficult to reverse what they have done.”
Conditions for Palestinians in the occupied West Bank deteriorated even further last month after a large-scale settler attack on the village of Tel, southwest of Nablus city, on July 24, during which four Palestinians and two Israeli settlers were killed.
Since the incident in Tel, settlers and soldiers have carried out daily, round-the-clock attacks, including mass shootings, physical assaults, arson, and land theft. Settlers have also erected at least 15 new colonial outposts on Palestinian land across the West Bank, with the vocal backing of top Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who announced a series of steps that included “accelerating the legalization of farm outposts and establishment of new ones.”
Back in Qusra, residents are terrified.
“I keep thinking about what happened to the Al-Tubassi family and praying that we can outlast this,” said Ruqayya.
Wadi, the Qusra mayor, is equally concerned. “We fear that this siege will become the new reality in the occupied West Bank, that Qusra will be another precedent for all the villages,” Wadi said. He also recounted that his older brother and nephew were murdered by armed settlers on October 12, 2023, during a funeral for four other Palestinians killed in the village also by settlers the prior day.
Some warn that the unrelenting settler-colonial violence may be reaching a tipping point. “The distance between the Palestinian people in the West Bank and massacres, is a question of when—not if,” said Abu Ghosh. “When the knife reaches the throats of Palestinians, they will have no choice but to resist with whatever means are available to them.”

reads.title: U.S. national debt tops $40 trillion; Russian strikes kill 16 in Ukraine; Ecuador’s intelligence chief killed in Kenya helicopter crash
reads.subtitle: Drop Site Daily: August 20, 2026
reads.body:
- People walk past damaged cars amid debris in a residential area hit by Russian strikes on August 20, 2026 in Kyiv, Ukraine. Photo by Ihor Kuznietsov/Global Images Ukraine via Getty Images.Thursday, August 20, 2026 – Fifty Bodies recovered in Gaza City. Report: 94% of households in Gaza need shelter aid. Human Rights Watch: Israeli settler violence has displaced 107 West Bank communities since 2023. Israel opens bidding for 1,234 units within settlement project, cutting northern West Bank from south. Israeli settlers injure nine Palestinians as attacks continue across occupied West Bank. World Central Kitchen condemns Israeli decision to close probe into killing of its workers in Gaza. President Donald Trump calls for “economic D-Day against Iran”; Iran calls it diversion from U.S. debt crisis. U.S. officials make dubious claims about Hormuz traffic. Iraq asks Iran for eased oil exporting rules. Ansarallah claims “comprehensive blockade” of Saudi tankers. Israel continues ceasefire violations with shelling and demolitions across southern Lebanon. Lebanese Parliament speaker “guarantees” U.S. that Lebanese Army can assert control over south if Israel withdraws. UNIFIL hands over Khardali-Litani position to Lebanese army ahead of mission’s end. U.S. national debt tops $40 trillion for first time. Trump pushes crypto industry's Clarity Act with ethics concerns looming. Los Angeles prosecutor reduces felony charges against officer who recorded colleagues’ bigoted remarks. Democratic-aligned “VoteVets” official also runs credit card industry lobbying front group. Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon calls Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu a “war criminal.” Syrian FM says Israel had “no justification” for bombing air base earlier this week. Ecuador's intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash. Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces see additional defections, Sudanese army claims. Russian missile strikes kill 16 amid Ukrainian interceptor shortage. Poland arrests Ukrainian man over alleged Russia-linked assassination plot. North Korea tests short-range ballistic missiles after U.S.-South Korea drills are scaled back.
This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday – Friday

## Palestine

- Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, 10 Palestinians were killed and 25 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

- The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,417 killed, with 174,360 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,283 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,248, while 813 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.

- Fifty Bodies recovered in Gaza City: Gaza Civil Defense crews recovered 50 bodies from beneath the rubble of the Al-Sawafiri, Al-Batniji, Karam, Harz, and Al-Af family homes in Gaza City after three days of work, the Palestine Information Center reported on Thursday.

- The Civil Defense agency said its teams have inspected eight completely destroyed homes where around 170 Palestinians are believed to remain buried, as recovery efforts continue while Israel obstructs the entry of equipment into the strip.

- Report: 94% of households in Gaza need shelter aid: An estimated 1.98 million Palestinians in Gaza, or 94% of the population, need shelter and basic household assistance, according to a new report by the Shelter Cluster, led by the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC).

- The report found that nearly two-thirds of households live in tents or makeshift shelters, structures that are not designed for long-term accommodation. More than half of households in tents had already used the same tent for over a year, while more than half of tents and makeshift shelters assessed were in poor or very poor condition.

- “A shelter is not adequate simply because it has four walls or a roof,” Jehan Salim, National Shelter Cluster Coordinator, said in a statement. “Ten months after the October 2025 ceasefire, most families have lived more than a year in shelters that were never designed for long-term accommodation. The materials needed to repair homes, restore basic services and provide improved shelters are still not entering Gaza at anything close to the scale required.”

- HRW: Israeli settler violence has displaced 107 West Bank communities since 2023: Israeli settler attacks have fully or partially displaced 107 Palestinian communities, comprising some 5,900 people, across the occupied West Bank since January 2023, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said in a new report. The Israeli military expelled another 32,000 Palestinians from their homes in the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams camps in January 2025. HRW said Israeli authorities are “arming, funding, and granting impunity” to settlers responsible for the attacks, which increasingly target Palestinians’ homes, land, livestock and access to water. The group cited OCHA figures showing an average of 6.6 settler attacks resulting in casualties or property damage per day in 2026—the highest rate it has recorded—and said at least 15 Palestinians, including two children, had been killed by settlers as of July 24.

- “The Israeli government and the settlers share the same goal of maximum land and minimum Palestinians,” HRW said.

- Israel opens bidding for 1,234 units within settlement project cutting northern West Bank from south: Israel issued a tender for the construction of 1,234 housing units in the E1 area east of Jerusalem, advancing a settlement project that would disrupt Palestinian territorial contiguity between Ramallah, East Jerusalem and Bethlehem, The Times of Israel reported. The units are part of roughly 3,400 homes approved last August, when Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said the project would “practically erase the two-state delusion.”

- The UN Secretary-General expressed “deep alarm” over the move, with his spokesperson warning that E1 would effectively “sever the connection between the northern and southern West Bank” and pose an “existential threat” to a two-state solution.

- The UK issued an unusually sharp response, summoning Israel’s chargé d’affaires and demanding the government immediately retract the tender and halt settlement expansion. Britain called the move “unacceptable and destructive” and said it “will not stand back and accept the destruction of the Two-State Solution.” The government also said it would announce a “comprehensive set of measures” in the coming weeks, including sanctions targeting those involved in illegal settlement expansion.

- Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar rejected the UK’s condemnation, claiming Jewish people have a right to live “throughout the Land of Israel,” and invoked the Balfour Declaration—a 1917 British imperial declaration backing the establishment of a Jewish national home in historic Palestine—to defend settlement in the occupied territory.

- Israeli settlers injure nine Palestinians as attacks continue across occupied West Bank:

- Ramallah: Five Palestinians were injured Thursday in a settler attack on a vehicle between Al-Mughayyir and Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, WAFA reported. Settlers attacked the vehicle, causing it to overturn, before assaulting those inside. Israeli authorities returned the body of a 17-year-old Palestinian boy, from Sinjil, after withholding it since he was killed by Israeli forces on March 17.

- Tubas: A Palestinian man was injured after settlers attacked him while he was working in the Al-Buqaia plain in the northern Jordan Valley.

- Hebron: Israeli forces transported several mobile homes to the newly established “Doron” settlement outpost on Mount Tarousa, west of Hebron. Israeli forces began excavation and land-clearing work there in June after armed settlers, under army protection, erected a tent and declared the establishment of the new settlement. Doron is among 19 new settlements approved by the Israeli government last year.

- Nablus: Settlers continued for a 12th consecutive day to besiege several homes in Qusra, south of Nablus, under Israeli army protection. Israeli forces raided Nablus city, Salem, Bazariya, Madama and Einabus, assaulting three Palestinians and detaining 10 others.

- World Central Kitchen condemns Israeli decision to close probe into killing of its workers in Gaza: World Central Kitchen (WCK) condemned the Israeli military’s decision to close investigations into the April 2024 strikes that killed seven of its workers. The army said Wednesday it reviewed 150 incidents of troop conduct in Gaza and only made decisions on five cases. It also closed investigations into two separate incidents that killed four Doctors Without Borders (MSF) employees in 2023 and 2024. At least 550 aid workers have been killed by Israel in Gaza since October 2023, almost all of them Palestinians.

- WCK said there was “never any excuse or justification” for the successive Israeli strikes on its clearly marked vehicles and accused the military investigation of muddying the events and shifting blame for the Israeli military’s conduct. The organization renewed its demand for an independent investigation, saying the Israeli military “cannot credibly investigate its own conduct.”

- Australia also condemned the decision, saying it was “outraged” that Israel would not pursue criminal proceedings over the killing of Australian WCK worker Zomi Frankcom and her six colleagues, with Foreign Minister Penny Wong announcing that Israel’s ambassador would be called in.

- Israeli human rights group B’Tselem called Israel’s rare internal investigations a “sham” that amount to a “a legal Iron Dome to protect Israeli soldiers from potential international legal consequences.”

- Netanyahu’s rival threatens strikes on Iran as candidates compete over who would wage more war: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett said Wednesday that, if he led the Israeli government, he would strike Iran in response to any attack by Hezbollah, claiming he would overhaul Israel’s security doctrine in the role.

- Bennett, one of Benjamin Netanyahu’s main political rivals ahead of Israel’s October election, served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022.

## Iran

- Trump calls for “economic D-Day against Iran”; Iran calls it diversion from U.S. debt crisis: President Donald Trump claimed he was about to undertake what he called “the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country” against Iran on Wednesday, vowing “economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale,” in a post on his Truth Social platform.

- Trump threatened that “any country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face tremendous economic consequences.” He cited as examples of support “oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, [and] front companies.”

- The warning indicates that Trump will impose additional sanctions on states and firms that keep trading with Tehran. As of Wednesday, no specific measures had been published by the Treasury Department, whose last Iran sanctions were announced on August 7.

- Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed Trump’s campaign against Iran as a diversion from America’s own crisis of “unprecedented debt” and surging interest costs. “Doubling down on failed policies will only bring further defeat—and enmity of Iranians,” Araghchi wrote in a post on X Thursday, sharing CNN and New York Times reports on the U.S. national debt surpassing a record $40 trillion and rising borrowing costs, adding that U.S. “economic terrorism threatens global economy and sovereignty worldwide.”

- U.S. officials make dubious claims about Hormuz traffic: Two U.S. officials told Axios on Wednesday that the U.S. military has been running a corridor through the Strait of Hormuz for weeks, moving about 10 million barrels of oil a day, roughly half pre-war volume, out of the Gulf via a southern channel off Oman.

- President Trump has said that “a tremendous amount of oil” is now leaving the strait and that the U.S. is not negotiating with Iran.

- Several energy analysts have questioned the 10 million figure, with Gregory Brew of Eurasia Group saying available data doesn’t corroborate it, and estimating flows at “at least 5-6 million bpd.” Rory Johnston suggested flows nearer to 5 million bpd, calling the 10 million figure a “stretch.”

- Iraq asks Iran for eased oil exporting rules: Iraq has asked Iran to grant its oil exports “special consideration” through the Strait of Hormuz, as disruptions to Gulf shipping continue to constrain Iraqi crude, Al-Monitor and the Iraqi News Agency reported on Wednesday.

- Iraqi Parliament Speaker Haibat Al-Halbousi made the request in talks with his Iranian counterpart Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Baghdad on Wednesday, saying Iraq was among the countries most affected by the regional crisis.

- Ghalibaf, who said Tuesday the strait would stay closed until the U.S. lifts its blockade, was in Iraq as part of a three-day visit to the country.

## Yemen

- Ansarallah claims “comprehensive blockade” of Saudi tankers: A spokesperson for Yemen’s Ansarallah claimed on Wednesday that the group had imposed a “comprehensive blockade” on Saudi ships, as part of its “siege for siege policy, ” arguing that its military strength had allowed it to more effectively deter Saudi attacks.

- The spokesman said the group had targeted eight Saudi oil tankers since its blockade began, five in the Red Sea and three in the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea, and turned back 48 others.

- In response to Saudi strikes on Sanaa airport and Hodeidah port, and airspace violations over Saada and Hajjah, the spokesman said the group carried out nine operations against Yanbu, Najran, Jizan, Abha, and Eastern Province oil facilities, and 14 more targeting Saudi forces at sites including Marib and al-Makha.

## Lebanon

- Israel continues ceasefire violations with shelling and demolitions across southern Lebanon: Israel continued its attacks across southern Lebanon on Thursday, carrying out a large explosion near Zawtar Al-Sharqieh in Nabatieh governorate, while renewed Israeli shelling struck Houla and the area between Talloussa and Markaba, also in Nabatieh governorate, according to Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA).

- Heavy Israeli artillery fire targeted Wadi Al-Salouqi, Wadi Al-Hujeir and valleys around Qabrikha and Touline, spanning Nabatieh and Bint Jbeil districts. In Tyre (Sour) governorate, Israeli forces carried out an explosion in the town of Mansouri.

- On Wednesday, Israeli forces carried out a wave of attacks and demolitions, striking Mansouri from the air, shelling Srebbine and blowing up homes in Zawtar Sharqieh, Tallouseh, Bani Hayyan, Houla and Khiam. In Mansouri, Israeli forces demolished and burned homes before renewed airstrikes later in the day.

- Parliament speaker “guarantees” U.S. that Lebanese Army can assert control over south if Israel withdraws: Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri said on Wednesday that the situation in southern Lebanon has become “unbearable” and is comparable to Gaza in the scale of Israel’s destruction, killings, and attacks on homes and heritage, L’Orient Today reported.

- Speaking to a delegation from the American Task Force on Lebanon (ATFL), Berri said the U.S. and President Trump were uniquely positioned to force Israel to end the war and withdraw to the international border.

- If Israel withdraws, Berri, Hezbollah’s chief political ally, said he would “guarantee the immediate deployment of the Lebanese Army” throughout the area south of the Litani River, with the army becoming the sole armed force responsible for security there.

- Separately on Wednesday, French President Emmanuel Macron invited the Lebanese government to a September 17 preparatory meeting in Paris ahead of an international conference aimed at supporting the Lebanese Army and Internal Security Forces. The conference, originally expected in March, was postponed following the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and Israel’s escalation of its war on Lebanon.

- UNIFIL hands over Khardali-Litani position to Lebanese army ahead of mission’s end: The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), the UN peacekeeping mission deployed in southern Lebanon since 1978, handed over its position near the Lebanese army post in the Khardali-Litani area to the army’s 7th Brigade, NNA reported. The transfer is part of a plan to hand a number of UNIFIL positions to the Lebanese army ahead of the mission’s scheduled termination at the end of this year.

## U.S. News

- U.S. national debt tops $40 trillion for first time: America’s gross national debt surpassed a record $40 trillion Wednesday, with the country on track to borrow more than $2 trillion this year alone amid spending on the Iran war and 2025 tax cuts. Rising interest payments now account for about half the country’s annual borrowing.

- Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who set a goal of cutting the deficit to 3% of GDP by 2028, acknowledged that the deficit is moving in the wrong direction this year.

- His department unexpectedly announced on Wednesday that it would “at least double” its long-dated debt buybacks, from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation, after yields on long-term government bonds surged to their highest levels in nearly two decades.

- The move, targeting 10- to 30-year debt, sent the 30-year yield down nearly 10 basis points and pushed the dollar sharply lower.

- Trump pushes crypto industry’s Clarity Act with ethics concerns looming: President Donald Trump called on Congress to pass the Clarity Act, a bill establishing federal regulatory rules for digital assets, at a White House event Wednesday attended by executives from Coinbase, Ripple, and other crypto companies.

- The bill would split crypto regulatory authority between the SEC and CFTC, impose anti-money-laundering rules, and ban senior officials, including the president, from creating digital assets while in office.

- Trump held this meeting and advocated for this legislation amid concerns about his personal ties to the industry, having taken in more than $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency-related ventures in 2025. The Trump family’s crypto business has expanded under his second term as well, with Trump’s World Liberty Financial company and personal meme coins having netted the family hundreds of millions of dollars each.

- LA prosecutor reduces felony charges against officer who recorded colleagues’ bigoted remarks: Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said Wednesday he would reduce felony charges against LAPD officer Daniel Flores, who secretly recorded 16 colleagues making racist, sexist, and homophobic remarks, to misdemeanor charges.

- Hochman, who was heavily criticized for his charging decision, maintained the recordings themselves violated California’s two-party consent eavesdropping law, though he called the comments themselves “abhorrent.”

- Flores, who taped co-workers 122 times over about a year before filing a complaint with the police commission in January 2025, will now be eligible for judicial diversion that could leave him with no criminal record if he avoids breaking the law for a year.

- Democratic-aligned “VoteVets” official also runs credit card industry lobbying front group: Peter Kauffmann, vice chair of the Democratic-aligned veterans group VoteVets and treasurer of its philanthropic arm, also serves as chief spokesperson for the Small Business Payments Alliance, a group funded by the credit card industry that fights to protect swipe fees charged by Visa and Mastercard, according to new reporting from The American Prospect.

- The Small Business Payments Alliance, a project of the credit-card-industry-funded Electronic Payment Coalition, has spent millions lobbying against the Credit Card Competition Act, and a report from Demand Progress found many of its member businesses have received funding directly from Mastercard, JPMorgan Chase, and Capital One.

- VoteVets’s political action committee has separately raised more than $20 million this year from billionaire donors to intervene in Democratic primaries favoring moderate, veteran-affiliated candidates over progressives, including $10 million spent boosting Iowa state Rep. Josh Turek over progressive Zach Wahls. Read the full report here.

- Florida Democratic Senate nominee Nixon calls Netanyahu a “war criminal”: Angie Nixon, who won Tuesday’s Democratic Senate primary in Florida, called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a “war criminal”  during on “Morning Joe” on Wednesday, saying he “needs to answer for his [crimes]” and that she opposes “sending any money or weapons to Israel at this moment.”

- “Right now, here in our state, in our country, we have veterans that are living unhoused on the streets,” Nixon said. “We have teachers that are calling my state office monthly because they can’t afford to live in the state of Florida anymore.”

- Analysis of Nixon’s victory published by the Washington Post on Wednesday found that she depended on a new coalition, performing strongest in counties that were younger, poorer, less college-educated and had larger Black populations. Nixon won the least college-educated and Blackest counties by roughly 30 points, carried counties with median household incomes below $65,000 by 20 points, and dominated areas with the largest shares of young adults.
📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill?  Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com

## Other International News

- Ecuador’s intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash: The director general of Ecuador’s intelligence agency (CIES), Michele Sensi-Contugi, was among seven dead as a result of a helicopter crash in central Kenya, officials said on Wednesday.

- The U.S. State Department confirmed five Americans were among the dead, including a Telemundo executive and a Miami restauranteur.

- The aircraft, carrying guests from the luxury tour operator &Beyond, crashed in the foothills of Mount Ololokwe in Samburu County. The cause of the crash remains under investigation.

- Sensi-Contugi, 42, appointed to lead Ecuador’s National Intelligence Center in 2024, was a close associate of right-wing President Daniel Noboa, a key U.S. partner in Washington’s militarized anti-cartel push.

- He and the CIES “served as architects of the political lawfare, police state, and brutal crackdown against journalists, indigenous members of the 2025 General Strike… and leftwing figures,” Drop Site contributor Camila Lourdes Galarza writes.

- Russian missile strikes kill 16 amid Ukrainian interceptor shortage: Russia launched a large-scale missile attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, firing dozens of cruise, ballistic and hypersonic missiles alongside 168 drones, killing at least 16 people and wounding more than 40. Ukrainian officials said 30 residential buildings, a school, children’s hospital, and kindergarten were damaged, while some 90,000 households temporarily lost power.

- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s dwindling stock of Patriot interceptors had not been replenished and accused allies of responding inadequately.

- A separate wave of attacks also struck infrastructure in Odessa, where repeated Russian attacks on ports and shipping have sharply disrupted Ukrainian agricultural exports.

- Poland arrests Ukrainian man over alleged Russia-linked assassination plot: Polish authorities arrested a Ukrainian man accused of trying to assassinate a representative of Ukraine’s arms industry in Irpin, near Kyiv, on behalf of Russian intelligence. Investigators said the suspect planted an improvised explosive device beneath the target’s car that was meant to be detonated remotely by cell phone but failed because of a malfunction.

- The suspect fled to Poland after the failed attack and was arrested in Warsaw, where he faces charges including attempted murder with explosives and could receive life imprisonment.

- RSF sees additional defections, army claims: Sudan’s army said 315 fighters from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces defected on Wednesday, led by Brig. Gen. Musa Khamiseen, as they crossed from North Darfur into Northern State before traveling under military intelligence escort to Omdurman, according to Sudan Tribune.

- Khamiseen’s reception by the army has drawn criticism from some of its Darfuri allies, who accuse him of involvement in summary executions and civilian killings during the RSF siege and capture of El Fasher last year.

- One fighter who was present during the siege accused Khamiseen of participating in killings near the earthen barricade erected to prevent civilians from fleeing and said he was filmed alongside Al-Fateh Abu Lulu, an RSF commander notorious for recording himself carrying out summary executions.

- North Korea tests short-range ballistic missiles after U.S.-South Korea drills are scaled back: North Korea launched roughly 10 short-range ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area toward its eastern waters, prompting South Korea’s national security council to hold an emergency meeting and call on Pyongyang to stop launches they say are prohibited by U.N. Security Council resolutions.

- The test came a day after the U.S. and South Korea announced they were reducing the size of the 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises after President Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon to “substantially reduce” the drills in an apparent attempt to revive diplomacy with Kim Jong Un.

- Syrian FM says Israel had “no justification” for bombing air base earlier this week: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani told Axios on Wednesday that Israel had no justification for bombing the Abu al-Duhur airbase, saying Damascus had explicitly informed Israel that no Turkish base or permanent Turkish troop deployment was planned there.

- Israel dropped at least eight bombs on the site on Tuesday, damaging newly rebuilt runways and hangars.

- Al-Shaibani said the base was largely empty and being rehabilitated for Syria’s air force, though Turkish officers had previously visited the site as part of broader military cooperation between the countries.

- Drop Site dispatch from Cuba: Amid a total oil blockade imposed by the U.S.—resulting in nationwide blackouts, medicine shortages, and disruptions to hospital operations—Cuba is transitioning away from fossil fuels toward renewable energy. Over 2,500 photovoltaic parks have been inaugurated across the country, a 96% increase over those built this time last year. Drop Site contributor Sasi Alejandre reports from Cuba, breaking down the country’s push toward an energy revolution; watch the video here.

reads.title: U.S.-Registered Drone Detected at Site of Suspected CIA Boat Strike
reads.subtitle: A drone registered to U.S. defense contractor Shield AI flew within 500 meters of Ecuadorian fishing boat hours after attack, according to flight data.
reads.body:
As a reader-funded independent news outlet, we operate free from the influence of governments, advertisers, and corporate backers. This is essential to our mission: to report on what matters most, beholden only to the truth. In that spirit, we made a commitment to ensure that our journalism is free for everyone, not locked behind a paywall. But that means we rely on the voluntary support of our community of readers. Please consider making a tax-deductible donation to support our work today.
Subscribe now

-
- An eyewitness watches the Negra Francisca boat burning on March 17, 2026 near the Galapagos Islands. Photo: Darwin Flores-Pico.QUITO, Ecuador—In the hours after a mysterious attack on an Ecuadorian fishing boat near the Galápagos Islands on March 17, a drone registered to U.S. defense contractor Shield AI was hovering just 500 meters from the burning vessel, La Negra Francisca, according to a review of flight tracking data by Drop Site News. This represents the first known vehicle to arrive at the site of the strike.
The unattributed bombing of three Ecuadorian fishing boats in January and March, and the subsequent abduction and torture of 36 fishermen, was first reported by Drop Site in April. Last week, The Washington Post, building on Drop Site’s ongoing investigation, reported that the attacks were part of a covert CIA operation.
According to flight and vessel tracking data from Radar 24 and Global Fishing Watch, the drone was a V-BAT model, primarily used for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance, but capable of carrying a weapons payload and switching its signal on and off to avoid detection.
The Shield AI drone matches the fishermen’s descriptions of the drones that circled their boats before the bombing, and bears the same red and green lights eyewitnesses reported seeing as they photographed the explosion.
Shield AI did not respond to a request for comment.
The CEO of Shield AI, Brandon Tseng, has publicly stated that the U.S. Coast Guard and Navy are using V-BAT drones “to interdict and destroy billions of dollars’ worth of drugs that were headed for the United States of America.” In 2024, the U.S. Coast Guard signed a $198 million contract with Shield AI for V-BAT drones; in April 2026, Shield AI announced it had received an $800 million contract for V-BAT drones from the U.S. Navy.
No drugs were found on any of the three fishing boats investigated by Drop Site—the Negra Francisca, Don Maca, and Fiorella—all of which were searched and cleared by Ecuadorian coast guard personnel prior to the strikes.
Last month, Drop Site published NASA thermal imagery consistent with an explosion at coordinates 1.5822°N, 87.6958W°, recorded at 1:02 p.m., the time fishermen say they were hit, and in the location where their transponder stopped broadcasting.
Tracking data suggests that the drone launched from a nearby boat on March 17, seven hours after the strike on La Negra Francisca and then circled near the site, its signal disappearing and reappearing. Ascending and descending patterns of movement indicate that the drone may have been landing on a boat and then resuming its flights.
Drop Site previously reported that vessel tracking data showed a U.S. Coast Guard cutter leaving a Galápagos military base a day before the Negra Francisca bombing—despite claiming it only deployed the cutter as a post-incident rescue effort. The Coast Guard vessel’s signal went dark and later appeared in Central American waters 24 hours before the fishermen were placed in El Salvador’s custody.
Video recordings, taken by eyewitnesses to the bombing, show the U.S. Coast Guard patrolling in the aftermath of the airstrike. Drop Site asked the U.S. Coast Guard in June to account for the cutter’s movements after its signal went dark. The Coast Guard responded that it “does not disclose cutter movements during law enforcement missions for operational security.”
In June, the U.S. Coast Guard told The Guardian it deployed its Bertholf cutter for a search-and-rescue operation after receiving a Mayday alert, contradicting prior statements by the U.S. Southern Command, which oversees maritime operations in the Pacific, that it had no knowledge of any U.S. involvement in the incidents. To date, the U.S. Coast Guard has not acknowledged using drones in its purported rescue efforts.
The U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Southern Command, and the Central Intelligence Agency did not respond to questions for this article.
While flight tracking data is recorded in UTC, dating the drone activity as March 18, in Galápagos time (UTC-06:00) both the strike and the subsequent drone activity occurred on March 17.

-
- Graphic: Tomi McCluskeyShield AI, a San Diego-based defense contractor, builds fighter jets and drones powered and piloted by artificial intelligence. The company was founded in 2016 with $1 million in seed funding from the Pentagon’s Defense Innovation Unit and the Naval Special Warfare Command. The Israeli military has reportedly used the company’s self-piloting drones for close quarters combat. V-BAT drones are also used by the Ukrainian military to identify Russian targets, as part of larger drone strike operations.

## Video of the burning fishing boat La Negra Francisca, taken by Darwin Flores-Pico, after the March 17, 2026 attack.

Last week, the New York Times and the Washington Post corroborated much of Drop Site’s original investigation of the attacks. In addition, the Times reported that a patrol plane flew from a military base in El Salvador in the direction of the three boats prior to each of the attacks. The Post identified that plane as FENIX 701, a Cessna business jet equipped with surveillance equipment operating out of Ilopango International Airport, which served as a hub for CIA operations during the Contra War against the Sandinista government of Nicaragua. The plane is registered to a company with virtually no digital footprint that lists its address as a mailbox inside a Virginia UPS store.
The FENIX 701 stopped broadcasting its signal well before reaching any of the boats and returned to base hours before the actual strikes, according to flight data.
The fishermen, like the airplane, eventually wound up in El Salvador. As Drop Site previously reported, men from the Negra Francisca and Don Maca boats were taken hostage by “gringo” gunmen in U.S. military uniforms who they say hooded, handcuffed, and starved them for eight days aboard their U.S.-flagged ship before turning them over to El Salvador’s navy hundreds of miles away from home.

-
- Graphic: Tomi McCluskeySince September 2025, the U.S. military has carried out over 66 strikes on vessels in the Caribbean and the eastern Pacific, killing at least 221, as part of Operation Southern Spear. The Trump administration has been boastful and unapologetic about this extrajudicial killing spree, which raises the question of why it would also run a covert CIA operation alongside it, as the Washington Post reported. There is precedent for such parallel operations, however. In April, for example, it was revealed that CIA agents were secretly working joint counter-narcotics raids with local agents in Mexico’s Chihuahua state without informing President Claudia Sheinbaum—despite her administration’s bilateral efforts with U.S. forces.
“We certainly do have cases in which one part of the U.S. government is doing something covertly while another part is doing something overtly,” Vincent Bevins, author of “The Jakarta Method,” a historical examination of the CIA’s Cold War operations, and editor of North South Notes, told Drop Site.
“That covert operation might be doing the same thing in a different way. It might be doing something similar and related,” Bevins added. “Even, at cross purposes, to some extent, with the official government line or official government policy….There are also cases where the only explanation is institutional chaos or poor planning.”

## A Community Under Siege
In June, Alexandra Bravo, a prosecutor investigating the U.S. strikes, was shot dead in the coastal city of Manta, the home port of the three fishing boats. U.S. troops have been deployed in Manta since December 2025, and the return of a de facto U.S. military base there—originally outlawed by the 2007 constitution and again ratified by 60% of Ecuadorian voters last November—evokes painful memories for residents who have not forgotten why it was banned in the first place: the U.S. publicly and brazenly sinking fishing ships off the coast of Manta.
Ecuador is under its 23rd martial law decree, which allows authorities to raid homes and wiretap communications without a warrant, and grants diplomatic immunity to all U.S. forces. President Daniel Noboa justifies the stripping of civil liberties as a necessary part of his “war on narcos.”
The strikes and subsequent abductions left Jordi Flores, a young crewmember aboard the Negra Francisca, with a severe foot injury and unable to work. Erik Coello, a crewmember aboard the Don Maca, which was also struck in March, suffers from 70% vision loss. And the families of the Fiorella, which vanished in January, have been crushed by grief for their missing sons, husbands, and fathers.

-
- Photo of Jordi Flores’ foot injury from the March 17 attack on the fishing boat La Negra Franscisca. Photo: Hernán Flores.Maria Mero, whose husband Gabriel Aladino Mero Delgado and brother Jefferson Ariel Mero Cueva both disappeared on the Fiorella, told Drop Site that her mother-in-law died awaiting her son’s return, falling into a deep depression and ceasing to eat in the weeks leading up to her death. Maria’s young daughter was hospitalized from the anxiety of going seven months without seeing her father. Gabriel’s disappearance also left a void in the family’s finances. Without him, Maria said, the ordinary necessities of life—groceries, her electricity bill, their daughter’s school uniform—are completely unaffordable.
“If the CIA or the United States or the El Salvador patrol or the president is reading this,” Maria said, “please, I beg you, return my husband, my brother, and all the people who are with them.”
