reads.title: Iran denies Trump’s claim of talks; Israeli strikes on Gaza kill over 30 since Friday “deal”; Cuba’s electricity collapses again
reads.subtitle: Drop Site Daily: August 3, 2026
reads.body:
- Displaced Palestinians inspect the destruction following an Israeli airstrike that targeted the nearby medical supplies warehouse of Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza Strip on August 1, 2026. Photo by Majdi Fathi/NurPhoto via Getty Images.This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday – Friday

## Iran

- Trump says U.S.-Iran talks will resume Monday; Tehran says no negotiations underway: President Donald Trump announced that renewed diplomatic negotiations with Iran would begin on Monday afternoon, claiming he had shelved plans for what he had previously described as “biggest attack since World War II.”

- Speaking to reporters onboard Air Force One, President Trump stated that the impending military operation was aborted at the last minute following direct appeals from key Middle Eastern allies, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE.

- He also told reporters that the talks would address the Strait of Hormuz and the “denuclearization of Iran.”

- Iran’s Foreign Ministry said Monday that Tehran is “not holding any negotiations with the United States at present,” stressing that ongoing talks are exclusively with Oman and focused on reaching “an understanding on the safe passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz,” Iran’s Mehr News Agency reported.

- At a weekly press briefing, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said that Iran “has never been the first party to violate any understanding,” adding that “the ball has been in the U.S. court for quite some time” after Washington announced on July 7 that it would no longer honor its commitments under the June 17 memorandum of understanding.

- Iran strikes Kuwait: Iran launched strikes toward Kuwait overnight Friday, Kuwait’s Defense Ministry reported, claiming that it disabled the wave of attacks.

- The ministry accused Iran of targeting several vital sites, including a government facility in northern Kuwait and civilian vehicles belonging to a company on Bubiyan Island.

- U.S. begins to withdraw from Erbil: The U.S. began withdrawing its remaining forces and heavy equipment from the military compound near Erbil airport on Saturday, including all Patriot air-defense batteries, as Washington approaches a September 30 deadline for a full troop pullout from Iraq, Al-Monitor reports.

- Sources said U.S. interceptors had stopped at least 95% of strikes targeting Erbil airport, leaving Kurdish officials concerned that the region is now more exposed. Remaining U.S. special forces may continue operating from smaller, low-profile locations in the country, an analyst said.

- NYT: U.S. dropped a 2,000-pound bomb on family in Qeshm:  Video, satellite imagery, and weapons analysis indicate the U.S. dropped a 2,000-pound bomb on a family home in a densely populated residential neighborhood on Iran’s Qeshm Island overnight Thursday, The New York Times reported on Saturday.

- The strike killed a husband, wife, and their 2-year-old son. Two other children, now orphaned, were pulled alive from the rubble.

- Iranian FM says Iran will respond “decisively” to attacks: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on Saturday that Iran is prepared to respond “decisively” to any U.S. aggression, according to the Iranian state-affiliated outlet Tasnim News.

- Araghchi held calls on Saturday with Pakistan Field Marshal Asim Munir, Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan, and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan to discuss the “destabilizing consequences” of U.S. actions in the region.

- Iran announces that it is near agreement for Hormuz control: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that talks with Oman over a mechanism to govern the strait are “nearing completion and in their final stages,” according to state news agency IRNA.

- Iran has previously demanded control over both of the northern and southern routes that transit the Strait, and has rejected a proposal from Oman and the U.S. that would give it control of only one.

- Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday that negotiations with Oman are focused on establishing a single, intermediate two-way shipping corridor to temporarily replace the existing northern and southern routes until a permanent Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS) is agreed upon.

- MBS notes Saudi concern about strikes on call with Trump:  Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman reportedly urged Trump to de-escalate and hold off on infrastructure strikes against Iran, asking for “clarity” on Trump’s war plans.

- The Wall Street Journal, however, reported on Sunday that the UAE lobbied President Trump to take “more decisive action” against Iran, arguing that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps would not compromise unless Washington escalated, took control of the Strait of Hormuz and potentially considered ground operations, the report says.

- Iran says several countries tell its FM they will not participate in future U.S. strikes: A spokesperson for Iran’s Foreign Ministry announced on Sunday that “in the past 24 hours,” representatives from the U.K., Bulgaria, and Ukraine had contacted the FM and said that they would not play any role in potential U.S. attacks on Iran.

- The FM noted in the same statement that any country that did participate in these strikes would “face Iran’s legitimate defense,” and noted that this included countries who “provided bases or military and logistical facilities” to the U.S.

- Two more executed in Iran: Iran executed two men on Monday convicted on charges of spying for Israel during both the June 2025 war and the ongoing conflict, according to the state affiliated news agency Mizan. The two men were identified as Omid Behzad and Pouria Safvat.

- Last week, Iran publicly hanged two men convicted of killing police officers during mass anti-government protests in January. At least 60 others convicted on charges related to the protests are at risk of execution, according to Amnesty International.

- “The Iranian authorities are unleashing a horrifying wave of executions and death sentences to punish and suppress dissent and project an image of strength and absolute control in the wake of the January popular uprising and amid ongoing attacks by U.S. and Israeli forces,” Heba Morayef, Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa at Amnesty International, said in a statement.

## Yemen

- Ansarallah will not charge for Bab Al-Mandab transit, officials say: Ansarallah’s maritime coordination body denied that it had plans to charge commercial vessels for passing through Bab Al-Mandab, and affirmed that transit through the waterway would remain free, The New Arab reported on Saturday.

- The body said the “safe transit service” it has devised in light of its embargo on Saudi shipping is voluntary and free.

- Officials warned shipping companies not to make payments to or share information with unauthorized parties.

- Two Saudi oil tankers transit Bab Al-Mandab despite Ansarallah blockade: Shipping data showed that two tankers carrying Saudi crude transited the Bab Al-Mandab Strait over the weekend despite Ansarallah’s declared maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia since July 20. According to Kpler data, the Suezmax tanker Lesbos, carrying about 1 million barrels of Saudi crude, and the VLCC DHT Vibhav, carrying 2 million barrels, both left the Red Sea with their Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders switched off.

## Palestine

- Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, 19 Palestinians were killed—18 in new attacks and one succumbing to wounds—and 35 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

- The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,375 killed, with 174,220 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,250 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,110, while 804 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.

- Israel kills 34 Palestinians, wounds 134 since Gaza deal announcement: Since Trump’s Friday announcement of a “historic agreement” and Hamas’s acceptance of phase two of the Gaza ceasefire deal, conditioned on Israeli compliance, Israeli attacks have killed at least 34 Palestinians and wounded 134 others across the Strip, according to Gaza’s Ministry of Health.

- An Israeli drone targeted the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood of Gaza City Saturday, killing two Palestinians and wounding several others, WAFA reported. An attack later on Saturday killed another Palestinian in the Sabra neighborhood.

- An Israeli drone strike on the Al-Mawasi area, near Khan Younis, killed one Palestinian and injured others Saturday.

- Also on Saturday, an Israeli drone struck Deir Al-Balah and killed four Palestinians, wounding others.

- Drop Site contributor Abdel Qader Sabbah filed a report from an attack near Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospital in Deir Al-Balah, which destroyed two central medicine warehouses, including critical equipment for kidney dialysis, and nearby tents sheltering displaced families. One resident asked, “What did we do to deserve this?” and noted that residents believed that the latest deal announced by Trump would improve their situation. “What did we do wrong?” she asked. “What did we do to deserve this, us and the dialysis patients? Who among us is guilty?” The full dispatch is available here.

- On Sunday, an Israeli strike on an apartment building in Gaza City killed two Palestinians, including a child, and wounded several others.

- A separate Israeli airstrike west of Khan Younis killed three members of a family, including a child. Another Israeli attack on Sunday afternoon in the area wounded five, three of whom were children.

- An Israeli attack on Sunday targeted an apartment building in Gaza City, killing an entire family of four, including a 5-year-old and an unborn baby that was reportedly ripped from its mother’s body by the force of the blast.

- Hamas issued a statement condemning the attacks on Sunday, noting that “criminal and frenzied bombardment” had killed 18 Palestinians since dawn and accusing Israel of deliberately escalating to sabotage the recently announced ceasefire agreement.

- Nickolay Mladenov, who leads the U.S.-backed “Board of Peace,” responded to the Israeli strikes by noting that the attacks had killed civilians and “destroyed medical supplies that people depend on,” without naming or condemning Israel.

- Senior Hamas official Basem Naim criticized the ongoing Israeli attacks: “At a time when Hamas demonstrated considerable flexibility and a high degree of responsibility by agreeing to the roadmap presented by the Board of Peace for the transition to the second phase of the Gaza War Termination Agreement, the Israeli occupation significantly escalated its targeting of civilians,” he said in a statement. “Its attacks have not ceased since the understandings were announced.”

- UN: 67% of Gaza faces food insecurity, 10% nears famine: The head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in the occupied Palestinian territory, Justin Brady, warned Monday that Gaza remains in a food emergency and is at risk of reaching Phase 5 of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), the threshold for an official famine declaration, Al Jazeera reported.

- Report: Israeli forces, settlers carried out 2,256 attacks in West Bank in July: Israeli forces and settlers carried out 2,256 attacks against Palestinians, their land, and property across the occupied West Bank in July, according to the Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. Israeli forces were responsible for 1,458 attacks and settlers for 798, the group said, describing the violence as a coordinated campaign in which the military provides “protection and support” for settler attacks.

- Settlers killed seven Palestinians in Nablus and Ramallah, uprooted, damaged, or poisoned 5,027 trees, damaged property in 440 incidents, and attempted to establish 29 new settlement outposts.

- Israeli authorities issued 33 military orders targeting more than 830 dunams (~205,000 acres) of Palestinian land and carried out 80 demolition operations, destroying 165 structures.

- Israel continues its attacks in the occupied West Bank:

- Ramallah: Israeli settlers beat and injured a Palestinian farmer and his wife in Beitillu on Saturday; footage published later showed bandages on the couple’s arms and legs. Israeli forces beat and pepper-sprayed at least three Palestinians, according to WAFA. A 19-year-old Palestinian was seriously wounded on Sunday after Israeli forces shot him in the thigh during a raid at the entrance to Jalazone refugee camp. Also in al-Mughayyir, an Israeli soldier on leave was arrested for allegedly taking part in the murder of a 10-year-old at a sheep farm outside of the town, according to Israel’s Kan Media.

- Nablus: Israeli forces issued a demolition order on Saturday for the family home of Faroukh Ramadan, the resident of Tal who defended himself by seizing the weapon of an Israeli settler who was pointing the gun at him, opening fire and killing the settler on July 24. Israeli settlers cut and damaged electrical poles in Madama, south of Nablus, on Sunday, WAFA reported, leaving residents without electricity. Israeli forces also conducted raids east of Nablus, breaking into several homes before dawn and detaining at least two residents.

- Tulkarm: Israeli forces ordered residents of the Jabal Al-Salihin area east of Nur Shams refugee camp Monday to evacuate their homes, citing planned military operations and possible explosions. The military also deployed bulldozers.

- Jenin: Israeli settlers destroyed part of a tobacco crop in the plain of Arraba on Saturday evening, WAFA reported, noting that settlers also hurled stones at Palestinian vehicles at a road leading into the village.

- Hebron: Israeli settlers carried out similar attacks in Idhna, throwing stones at cars while receiving protection from the Israeli military. Israeli forces detained 11 Palestinians working the fields in the village of Khashem al-Daraj, near Yatta, on Saturday.

- Occupied East Jerusalem: Israeli settlers attacked the Armenian Church in the Old City on Sunday, throwing stones and collectively spitting at its entrance, according to WAFA.

- Israel agreed to halt attacks, Palestinian close to Kushner claims: Mohammad Dahlan, the exiled former Fatah security chief in Gaza who is based in the UAE and has emerged as an influential figure in post-war planning, said Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and lead Gaza mediator, assured him he reached an agreement with Israel to cease the assaults starting Sunday morning, as part of the roadmap deal Hamas and other factions approved this week.

- Dahlan later deleted the portion of the tweet mentioning a U.S. agreement with Israel to end its attacks.

- Israel says it will not withdraw from Gaza despite agreement: The Israeli Prime Minister’s Office issued on Sunday its first public reaction since U.S. President Trump announced the Board of Peace agreement with Palestinian resistance factions earlier this week, saying that Israel would not withdraw from Gaza and claiming it had “serious” concerns about Hamas’ continued operations in the Strip and potential to “expand” absent an Israeli presence.

- Israel has reportedly demanded continued freedom to strike and kill Palestinians in Gaza as part of the newest agreement, according to the AP.

- Israeli court freezes Ben Gvir plan for crocodiles in prison moat over animal rights concerns: An Israeli court on Sunday imposed a temporary injunction freezing a plan by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir to place crocodiles in moats around Ketziot Prison where Palestinians are held following a petition by the animal rights group Let Animals Live. The petition requested that crocodiles be reclassified as a protected species. “The claims regarding the expected harm to the crocodiles merit investigation and justify issuing an order prohibiting the transfer,” Judge Avraham Rubin wrote in the ruling, according to Times of Israel.

- Family of Palestinian in viral photo of Israeli soldiers mocking him appeals for urgent action: The family of Mahmoud Al-Drimli, the Palestinian identified as the blindfolded man in a widely circulated photograph with two female Israeli soldiers smiling next to a detained Mahmoud, has appealed for urgent international intervention to determine his fate and secure his release nearly two years after he disappeared while attempting to return to Gaza City.

- The family called on the International Committee of the Red Cross, the United Nations, and humanitarian organizations to intervene and ensure his physical and psychological safety and work toward his release.

- His parents previously told Drop Site they have received no information about him since his disappearance in November 2024.

## Lebanon

- Israeli phosphorus attacks hit southern Lebanon despite ceasefire:

- Overnight, Israeli warplanes struck the Ali Al-Taher heights on the outskirts of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa. Forces fired phosphorus munitions that ignited fires in olive groves and pine forests around Yaroun and the city of Bint Jbeil.

- Israeli artillery shelled Mais Al-Jabal in the Marjayoun district, Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA) reported, while an Israeli drone dropped a stun grenade on a pickup truck in Al-Mansouri in Tyre district, setting it ablaze.

- Lebanon-Israel talks progressing while blast wounds five Lebanese soldiers: U.S. Ambassador Michel Issa said he is encouraged by ongoing negotiations in Rome between Lebanon and Israel, according to the NNA. Issa said “significant technical work” remains to ensure civilian safety and stressed that “there is a meaningful difference between drafting an agreement on paper and implementing it responsibly.”

- Separately, the Lebanese Army said five soldiers were wounded while accompanying civilians in Kafr Kila in Bint Jbeil district on Sunday. The army later said an investigation determined the explosion was caused by a “suspicious object” and was continuing to determine the remaining circumstances. Israel’s military claimed the explosive device belonged to Hezbollah.

- An Israeli officer was wounded overnight Saturday during what the Israeli military described as a “close-quarters encounter” with Hezbollah fighters in southern Lebanon, AFP reported. The military said the officer was injured during “operational activity” in the area, without providing further details.

## U.S. News

- Major primary contests set for Michigan, Missouri, Washington state, Kansas, Virginia: The most-watched race Tuesday is the Senate contest between Dr. Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens. Polls show El-Sayed with a double-digit lead over Stevens despite more than $60 million being spent to boost Stevens and blunt El-Sayed. For context, $60 million is several times more than the entire Democratic National Committee has in cash on hand. More than $30 million of that spending comes directly from United Democracy Project (UDP), the super PAC set up by AIPAC.

- In Mid-Michigan, Will Lawrence, another anti-genocide candidate opposed by pro-Israel money, is leading in the polls against two centrist opponents. Meanwhile, a bizarre influx of money from what appears to be a Republican-linked super PAC has come in last-minute to boost Lawrence.

- In Detroit, state Rep. Donovan McKinney, with the backing of DSA, Justice Democrats, and American Priorities (the anti-AIPAC PAC) is challenging incumbent Rep. Shri Thanedar. Polls have McKinney trailing but volunteers are flooding into Detroit to get out enough of the vote to overcome the remaining margin. The race is expected to be very close.

- In St. Louis, former Rep. Cori Bush is in a rematch against AIPAC-backed Wesley Bell. Bush remains an underdog, but a strong anti-establishment wave could be enough to carry her back into office.

- Rep. Haley Stevens features pastor with anti-LGBTQ, Islamophobic history in Michigan Senate ad: Days before Michigan’s Tuesday Democratic Senate primary, Representative Haley Stevens released a campaign ad featuring Bishop Christopher Martin of Flint’s Cathedral of Faith Ministries, who has a history of anti-LGBTQ sermons and recently shared Facebook posts warning of a “Muslim takeover” in the U.S., The Lever reported.

- Martin, who told The Lever he has been “working with Haley Stevens” and is “glad to be in the ad,” defended his past comments, saying he is “not homophobic” but does not believe gay people should serve as pastors.

- Justice Department scraps parts of Trump’s IRS deal to save Blanche’s AG confirmation: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the Justice Department is abandoning key elements of the settlement it struck with Trump over his lawsuit against the IRS, bowing to demands from Republican Sens. John Cornyn and Thom Tillis who had threatened to block his confirmation.

- Blanche posted a signed memo formally nullifying the $1.8 “anti-weaponization fund,” which would have paid allies of Trump who claimed that they were persecuted by the government, and a second statement narrowing immunity previously granted to Trump’s entire family and several associates to Trump, two of his sons, and the Trump Organization.

- The move comes days before the Senate Judiciary Committee is set to vote Tuesday on Blanche’s nomination.

- Sen. Bernie Moreno calls former son-in-law Rep. Max Miller “unfit for office”: Ohio Republican Senator Bernie Moreno publicly spoke out against his former son-in-law Rep. Max Miller (R-Ohio) for the first time on Sunday, writing on X that Miller, “fails” basic character standards for elected officer, that he “holds [his] breath every minute he has custody of [Moreno’s] granddaughter,” and calling for Miller to “seek professional help.”

- Miller has been accused by his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, of throwing hot water from a skillet at her body, and of holding a gun to her head. She has also accused him of fracturing their young daughter’s collarbone. He denies the allegations. Miller was also accused of abusing Stephanie Grisham, a former White House press secretary, during a relationship the two had while both worked in the White House.

- Democrats have called for a House Ethics Committee investigation, while most Republicans, including Rep. Jim Jordan, have defended Miller or stayed silent. Miller’s re-election has also come into question, with his formerly safe Republican seat now viewed as a “toss-up.”

- Education Secretary Linda McMahon asks universities to commit to reforms by end of 2026: McMahon sent a letter on Monday to U.S. university leaders asking them to reexamine admissions practices, hire more conservative faculty, crack down on student protests, reduce foreign donations, and lower tuition, according to Bloomberg News.

- The letter, which was drafted with input from the Association of American Universities, carries no direct penalties for noncompliance, though a White House official said schools that do announce reforms may have more influence over the roughly $200 billion federal research funding system.

- Author of DNC autopsy says party buried chapter questioning Biden’s 2024 run: Paul Rivera, the author of the Democratic National Committee’s unfinished 2024 election autopsy, told The New York Times on Sunday that a chapter titled “What Happened in 2024”—which questioned President Joe Biden’s decision to seek re-election and criticized Democratic strategists that grew “generationally wealthy” off politics—was omitted from the draft the party released in May.

- DNC chair Ken Martin denied Rivera’s account, saying in a written statement that he was never given the chapter and that it was not found in an extensive search of party files.

- Senate appropriators unveil stopgap bill to avert shutdown: Senate appropriators released text Sunday of a bipartisan stopgap funding bill that would keep federal agencies funded through December 11 at current levels and delay broader budget negotiations until after the November midterms.

- The bill includes a temporary ban on a White House proposal to let political appointees approve federal grants.

- Unlike the House version, the Senate plan bars new funding for immigration enforcement agencies and omits major funding increases for the military sought by the Trump administration.
📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill?  Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com

## Other International News

- Drone strikes Russian Black Sea resort, killing six: Russian authorities said a drone struck a crowded beach near the resort town of Gelendzhik in the southern Krasnodar region on Monday, killing six people, including three children, and injuring roughly 40 others.

- The regional governor accused Ukraine of deliberately targeting civilians, while a Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson called the attack terrorism. Ukraine did not immediately comment, and the origin of the drone remains unconfirmed.

- Suicide bombing kills 17 outside police station in northwest Pakistan: An explosion outside a police station in Swat’s Kabal area killed 17 and wounded at least 34 on Sunday, according to police and rescue officials. Seven police officers were among the dead, and authorities believe one of those killed was the bomber.

- A rally by local residents supporting the police was underway nearby.

- The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan claimed responsibility for the attack in a statement issued after the bombing.

- Read Drop Site’s report on the Pakistani military’s violent crackdown on a protest movement in Kashmir.

- Cuban electricity grid collapses again: Cuba’s electrical grid collapsed Sunday night, cutting power across the island in the latest of several nationwide failures this summer. The state electricity utility did not immediately identify the trigger or provide a restoration timetable.

- The grid had already collapsed three times over nine days in July, including an outage that affected roughly 10 million people.

- Washington’s oil blockade following the U.S. seizure of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro cut off supplies from Cuba’s principal oil provider; Mexican shipments have also stopped under U.S. pressure.

- Colombian President Gustavo Petro visited Cuba in a show of solidarity where he called on Trump to engage in dialogue and find a diplomatic solution.

- Trump’s shadow envoy in Venezuela is out: Mauricio  Claver-Carone, the Miami businessman operating as Donald Trump’s informal Caracas envoy, has stepped down. Following the U.S. capture of  Maduro, Claver-Carone shaped Venezuela policy, brokered corporate access to oil reserves, and steered lucrative contracts without an official government role.

- Claver-Carone claims he voluntarily handed control to standard diplomatic channels, but administration sources say he was pushed out. State Department and White House officials reportedly grew tired of his heavy-handed style, reliance on shadowy intermediaries, and the chaotic corporate feeding frenzy surrounding the intervention, according to Reuters.

- Taiwan defense chief states that U.S. military ties are “far closer” than publicly understood: Taiwanese Defense Minister Wellington Koo said cooperation with the United States is “far closer than many people imagine,” citing expanding exchanges with U.S. Indo-Pacific Command at multiple levels to strengthen the island’s combat readiness.

- China has intensified naval, air and coast guard operations around Taiwan, including along its Pacific coast, prompting Taiwanese exercises preparing for a possible blockade.

- Sudanese army drone strike on a community court in Darfur kills at least 35: At least 35 people were killed and others wounded when drones belonging to the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) struck a customary court in the village of al-Zawiya Ghara, in

reads.title: How a Squandered Democratic Trifecta Is Pushing Michigan Left
reads.subtitle: Anti-establishment candidates aim for a sweep across more than a dozen Michigan races in Tuesday's primary.
reads.body:
Polls close throughout most of Michigan at 8 p.m. ET tomorrow, and results in the closely watched race between Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens will be coming in quickly. In Missouri, Cori Bush is locked in a rematch with Rep. Wesley Bell, who knocked her out of Congress with a then-record-setting amount of money from AIPAC. In Michigan and also in Washington state and Virginia there are a number of other critical races we’ll be watching.
On Tuesday morning at 9:30 am ET, we’ll be hosting our regular livestream on YouTube and Twitter. Then on Tuesday evening at 7:30 pm ET we’ll go live with Krystal Ball at both the Drop Site and Breaking Points YouTube pages, and we’ll track the results until we have a winner.  We’ll have a number of interesting guests coming through, though I don’t want to make any promises, because election nights can be chaotic. Tune in if you can. Either way, we’ll be watching a historic night unfold.
As always, we can’t do this without your support. If you haven’t yet become a paying subscriber, please consider doing so.
Or you can make a deductible contribution here.
— Ryan Grim
Subscribe now

-
- U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens hosts a campaign event with former House Majority Whip Congressman Jim Clyburn (left) and Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer (right) at Michigan Conference-Teamsters on July 24, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. Photo by Bill Pugliano/Getty Images.Story by Tom Perkins
More than a dozen anti-establishment candidates running on populist economics and Israel policy are threatening to take seats now held by Democrats across Michigan, from U.S. Senate to city councils.
A sweep or strong showing by these insurgents in Tuesday’s primary would be seismic, upending Democratic Party power dynamics in an establishment stronghold. More broadly, if the Democratic Tea Party comes for the bellwether state of Michigan, the results would show that a new bottom-up politics is taking root, providing the clearest signal yet that the fundamental shift in the party underway is not restricted to New York or heavily blue cities.
(A full list of the races to watch on Tuesday, plus a handful already concluded, is at the end of this story.)
To understand the moment here, one needs to look at the night of November 8, 2022, when midterm returns trickling in across Michigan slowly began to reveal a surprise result: Democrats had won a trifecta and gained control over the state government for the first time in 40 years.
To many in the party, it felt like the state was emerging from the darkness after decades of being unable to legislate under one of the nation’s most gerrymandered maps, suffering under GOP governors like Rick Snyder, architect of the Flint water crisis.
This kind of coverage matters. Make sure we can keep doing it:
Rank-and-file Democrats expected that wildly popular proposals they supported would move easily into policy: making corporations pay for pollution, taxing the wealthy, dramatically expanding healthcare, addressing the soaring cost-of-living for the working class, and reining in DTE Energy, among the nation’s most expensive and unreliable utilities.
These proposals did not pass. Most of the economic agenda died. No one was held responsible for Flint.
Pro-business Democrats in leadership positions, including Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, thwarted the most meaningful proposals while cutting the Covid safety net. The largely squandered trifecta and failure to address Michigan’s most urgent economic needs infuriated the base.
The party’s failures to enact popular legislation dovetailed with outrage over the establishment’s attacks on pro-Palestinian advocates and disrespect of Michigan’s huge Arab-American populations; centrist Democratic support for an onslaught of data center plans in the state; and the relentless prioritization of corporate interests over residents’ needs. The state’s powerful unions began inching away from corporate Democrats.
This confluence of forces ignited the groundswell of support for the 15 grassroots change candidates now on the ballot. Some have already won this cycle, and the rest may make major gains on Tuesday.
Yousef Rabhi is a Democratic Socialist of America (DSA) member aiming to unseat a 12-year party machine mayor in Ann Arbor, the state’s most liberal big city. He is up 13 points per a late July poll.
“Ultimately a lot of the major landmark legislation that they promised just did not get delivered,” he told Drop Site. “Now there’s this combination of rank-and-file working people, progressive activists and folks from all over the political spectrum, people from Black, Arab, Jewish communities, who are feeling overlooked by Democratic party right now, and there is surge surge of left candidates where there is disaffection.”
In the race for U.S. Senate, the latest polls put former Detroit health department director Abdul El-Sayed up by 10-15 points over Rep. Haley Stevens despite at least $30 million in spending by pro-Israel groups. The Bernie Sanders-endorsed, former Sunrise co-founder William Lawrence is up 15-25 points in a mid-Michigan U.S. House seat, though establishment polling has him behind. Donovan McKinney, backed by Justice Democrats and Sanders, was running slightly behind the AIPAC-backed incumbent Shri Thanedar in a poll on the Detroit U.S. House district race.
Downballot, former Uncommitted Movement co-founder and Sanders endorsee Abbas Alawieh is attempting to be the first Arab-American to serve in the state senate, and to represent Dearborn, a city with a huge Lebanese-American population. Alawieh previously served as a congressional aide to Reps. Andy Levin and Rashida Tlaib of Michigan, as well as Cori Bush — who is mounting her own comeback bid in St. Louis on Tuesday. In a Detroit state house district, Chris Gilmer-Hill, backed by the DSA and Working Families Party, is running against State Rep. Helena Scott, a pugnacious machine politician.
But the insurgents face headwinds. The congressional races are awash in corporate and pro-Israel lobby money. Pro-Israel donors are opposing leftist Yemeni-American state Senate candidate Abe Aiyash, and they account for about one-third of the $353,000 raised by his opponent, the establishment-backed Justin Onwenu.
Meanwhile, many older, conservative black voters here have rejected Sanders-style politics, and division exists among them and Arab-Americans. The left has also been so weak in Michigan that there is little infrastructure like that which the DSA and Working Families Party laid for many years in New York that was essential to Zohran Mamdani’s win, and the June “socialist sweep.”
Still, the Working Families Party and DSA are both gaining strength and active this cycle. And there may be an “Abdul effect,” said Bernie Porn, a state pollster with EPIC-MRA: “El-Sayed’s strength will probably translate into strength for all anti-establishment candidates.”

## Gaza and Economic Frustration Dovetail
The Democratic trifecta culminated with an acrimonious intra-party lame duck fight at the end of 2024, as pro-business Democrat House Speaker Joe Tate sat on popular bills, including nine that passed the legislature. Among them, legislation to lower healthcare costs for unions, expand working class tax credits, address predatory debt collectors, and fund an African-American history museum.
Democrats had lost the house in the November election, and instead of sending the bills to Whitmer for a signature before the trifecta ended, Tate handed them to incoming GOP leadership, which also refused to send them to the governor.
The state supreme court, controlled by Democrats, ruled several weeks ago that the bills had to be sent to Whitmer for signatures. Instead, Whitmer quickly vetoed them.
Labor viewed Whitmer’s move as a “betrayal,” a top official with one of the state’s largest unions, who declined to use their name to speak freely, told Drop Site. Michigan is a labor stronghold, but 50 years of establishment policies weakened it. Too many Democrats still try to “walk the line” between corporate and labor interests, the union official said.
“When we took back the trifecta for the first time in 40 years, it was great that the party in charge shifted, but the reality is that the largest corporations in the state still were the ones who were setting the agenda at the governing table,” the union official added.
Increasingly, the union has a hardline position, the official added: “You fight for workers or you do the bidding of corporations, but you cannot do both as Democrats have tried, and there’s a reckoning right now because of that.”
However, there is no labor effort to support “leftist” candidates, the official said. Instead, they back candidates who unequivocally choose workers over corporate interests. In Michigan, that more frequently means candidates like El-Sayed, who also received a major endorsement from the American Federation of Teachers that is part of the AFL-CIO, and even a Wayne County Sheriff’s Office union. Rabhi, a union member who has joined others on the picket line, has support from the local teachers’ union that has never previously endorsed in a mayoral race, he said. Local chapters of AFSCME and the UAW have also endorsed him, as have the AFT and National Nurses’ Union, among others.
This translates into material support on the ground. Earlier this year, in Three Rivers—the type of small, west Michigan town where El-Sayed needs to do well to win the nomination—he joined a UAW picket line. The union won an $8 per hour raise in a 10-day strike, and, in response, the union mobilized a door knocking campaign for El-Sayed, who won over some Trump voters there.
The UAW also took a surprise step in voting to divest from Israel over its genocide, which drew retribution from the Trump administration. Meanwhile, economic discontent among Michigan’s Arab-American and Muslim communities added to frustration over establishment hostility to Arab-Americans and pro-Palestinian advocates.
The establishment ignored the 100,000 “uncommitted votes” in Michigan’s 2024 Democratic presidential primary, and steadfastly refused to change course on its support for Israel’s genocide. Though no data on how many uncommitted voters did not vote for Kamala Harris in the general exists, she lost the state by 80,000 votes, and election data showed a loss of about 22,000 votes in the three cities with the highest Arab-American and Muslim populations alone.
It appears the establishment learned little. It launched attacks in late March against El-Sayed for campaigning with Hasan Piker, broadly over their criticisms of Israel. The media attacks, led by State Sen. Mallory McMorrow, then El-Sayed’s opponent, came as Israel was invading Lebanon, and destroying cities in which many local Lebanese-Americans have roots, family members, and friends. Some community leaders warned that the Democratic establishment was ignoring their pain, and making the same mistakes as 2024.
Weeks later, Gaza and economic discontent drove upsets at a contentious April Democratic nominating convention, where leftist, pro-Palestinian attorney Amir Makled beat the pro-Israel, establishment candidate Jordan Acker for University of Michigan regent. Acker had led the U-M attack on pro-Palestinian students. And Eli Savit, a progressive prosecutor, defeated the corporate, pro-Israel-backed Karen MacDonald for the state attorney general.
Within months of the Piker controversy, McMorrow dropped out as she lagged in the polls, and El-Sayed broke out as the front runner.
The economic frustration is not separate from dismay over establishment support for Israel for Arab-American and Muslim voters here, and Gaza is many issues wrapped into one, said Bilal Baydoun, a political analyst in Dearborn.
“Supporting the genocide in Gaza is a statement on where Democratic priorities are and it’s an identifier where people say ‘Look they’re sending billions of dollars to Israel, and I haven’t heard of anything they’re doing for my kids,’” Baydoun said. “People say ‘I was able to afford a home in my country—I don’t think my kid can do that anymore.’”
A survey conducted in April, sponsored by Drop Site News and Zeteo, found that 62% of Michigan Democratic primary voters agreed that they are less likely to trust a candidate would stand up for Michiganders in general if they won’t stand up to AIPAC; 13% disagreed with this sentiment.

## Can Anti-Establishment Candidates Win in Detroit and Ann Arbor?
In Ann Arbor, where Rabhi and a slate of four other candidates are attempting to put a major dent in the corporate political machine that has ruled for 12 years, voters’ concerns are a microcosm of the state and federal levels.
“People say that for 12 years the rent has gone up, the cost of living has gone up, the roads have fallen apart, and city services have not been meeting the needs of the residents,” Rabhi said.
But Michigan is a diverse state and though the 15 candidates generally support the same policies, campaigning on the east side of Ann Arbor may look different than on the east of Detroit.
One recent poll shows El-Sayed behind in Detroit 66-33. Part of this may be the conservative older population. And tensions exist between Black people and Arab-Americans in Detroit, which in part stems from anger with gas station, party store, and grocery store owners in the city who are largely Chaldean and are accused of mistreating their mostly Black customers.
Some, like Eboni Taylor, a Sanders endorsee running for in a state Senate district on Detroit’s largely Black east side, actively avoid the “leftist” label, and make clear they do not have an association with the DSA.
While campaigning, Taylor talks about maternal health, bringing down childcare costs, and rejecting corporate money because “these are common sense things that people want,” Taylor said. “Working class families are waiting their turn to be heard and for policy to work for them, and that’s what is resonating for them with my campaign.”
When she navigates nursing homes or other areas where her list of progressive endorsements does not carry a lot of currency, she connects with people by talking about her history in the Baptist church, struggles raising kids, and watching her working class parents who still live in the same east side home build a better life for her.
However, Detroit City Council Member Denzel McCampbell, a former spokesperson for Rep. Rashida Tlaib, openly campaigned and won this cycle as a DSA member in a largely Black, low-income district on Detroit’s west side, and survived his opponents attacking him for being socialist.
“On the doors, what it meant to be a socialist did not come up - what came up is ‘You’re not going to sell us out, right?’” McCampbell said. “That’s what’s connecting—‘Are you going to be an authentic leader that fights for us?’”

## Key Michigan races:

- Abdul El-Sayed versus Rep. Haley Stevens for U.S. Senate.

- Bernie Sanders-endorsed former Sunrise co-founder William Lawrence is running against two establishment candidates, Matt Maasdam and Bridget Brink in the 7th Congressional district.

- Justice Democrats/Sanders-backed Donovan McKinney is running against the AIPAC-backed incumbent Shri Thanedar in the 3rd Congressional district.

- DSA member U.S. Rep. Rashida Tlaib is running for re-election against the establishment-backed Inkster Mayor Byron Nolen in the 12th Congressional district.

- Uncommitted co-founder and Sanders-endorsed Abbas Alawieh is running against state Rep. Erin Byrnes in Michigan state Senate district 2.

- Leftist former state Rep. Abe Aiyash is running against establishment pick Justin Onwenu in Michigan state Senate district 1.

- Sanders-endorsed Eboni Taylor is running against a long list of establishment-backed candidates in Michigan State Senate district 3, including Whitmer administration veteran Korey Hall.

- DSA and WFP-backed Chris Gilmer-Hill is running against incumbent state Rep. Helena Scott in Michigan state House district 8.

- Progressive prosecutor Eli Savit beat the establishment and pro-Israel-backed candidate, Karen McDonald, for state attorney general at the April Democratic nominating convention.

- Leftist, pro-Palestinian attorney Amir Makled beat the establishment, pro-Israel-backed candidate, Jordan Acker, for U-M board of regents at the April Democratic nominating convention.

- DSA member Yousef Rabhi is running for mayor of Ann Arbor with a slate of four other leftists candidates who are running for city council seats. Chris Taylor is the incumbent mayor.

- DSA member and former Tlaib staffer Denzel McCampbell won a seat on the Detroit City Council in late 2025, defeating former state Rep. Karen Whitsett.

- DSA State Rep. Dylan Wegela, WFP-backed State Rep. Tonya Phillips, and WFP-backed Jason Morgan are all defending seats in the Michigan House.

reads.title: Ceuta: Did Israel and US engineer the crisis?
reads.subtitle: Israel and the US exploited the Ceuta crisis. But did their involvement go further?
reads.body:
- Last Thursday and Friday, around 60,000 people crossed from Morocco into Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta, almost doubling its population. Many of them swam. At least 72 died in the attempt.
Almost all have since returned to Morocco. But the episode provoked a major crisis for Spain’s government. Other European countries turned on Madrid, claiming that its migration policy was responsible. Italy’s hard-right government temporarily reintroduced border controls on arrivals from Spain.
The far right across Europe and the wider West was jubilant. Here, they claimed, was proof of their narrative about a migrant invasion of Europe – and of the supposedly inevitable consequences of Spain’s progressive government taking a more humane approach to migration.
Help us take on the Establishment media by becoming a free or paid subscriber.

## The far right seizes the crisis
Spain’s far-right Vox party called the crossings an “invasion”, demanded the complete closure of the border and linked the migrants to sexual violence and stabbings. Vox could be in government next year through a coalition with the hard-right People’s Party.
Donald Trump similarly declared that the crossings “look like an invasion”, before turning the deaths and desperation in Ceuta into a campaign message:

> “That same thing’s going to happen to us if the Republicans don’t get elected, except worse.”
The US State Department went further:

> “This unacceptable incident is the direct result of the Spanish Government’s deliberate efforts to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe.
“We are considering actions to defend Americans at home and abroad from this threat and stand ready to assist other European allies considering similar options.”
Vice-President JD Vance posted:

> “Thank God @POTUS was elected and our country’s border no longer looks like this.
“These images out of Spain are an unfortunate reminder of the consequences of mass migration and the radical left-wing globalist policies that have enabled the Invasion of the West.”
Nigel Farage, the leader of Britain’s hard-right Reform UK, declared: “This is battle for the future of our civilisation.”
Other Reform politicians joined in. Suella Braverman claimed: “Make no mistake, these men are on their way to the UK right now.”
This was totally false. Almost all of the migrants have already been returned to Morocco.
Before turning to what actually happened – and to what could suggest possible Israeli and American involvement – it is worth challenging the claim that Spain somehow brought this crisis on itself through its migration policy.
Share

## Spain did not cause this crisis
Pedro Sánchez’s government has introduced a regularisation programme under which undocumented migrants can apply for one-year residence and work permits, provided they had lived continuously in Spain for at least five months before 1 January 2026.
The purpose was straightforward: to bring migrant workers out of the shadow economy and into legal employment, where they could pay taxes, exercise basic rights and play a full part in Spanish society.
Unlike so many other European leaders, Sánchez was prepared to tell people the truth. Welcoming migrants, he has previously said, was “an essential step to guarantee the prosperity and sustainability of our welfare state”.
But the regularisation programme had nothing to do with those attempting to enter Ceuta. None of them qualified for it.
Italian politicians and others across Europe claimed that Spain’s policy would unleash a new wave of migration into their own countries. That was simply false. The permits applied only to residence and employment in Spain. They did not grant the right to work elsewhere in Europe.
Nor did reaching Ceuta provide an automatic route to the Spanish mainland. Those crossing the border would still face extensive further legal and physical barriers before they could travel across the Strait of Gibraltar.
The politicians pretending otherwise were not confused. They were cynically exploiting public ignorance about how the system works – and the hostility towards migrants that such ignorance can so easily be used to inflame.
It is true that Spain’s Supreme Court – acting independently of the government – had ruled that people arriving by water could not be subjected to the exceptional “hot return” policy used at land fences.
But it did not prevent Spain from returning migrants. In practice, it offered those crossing into Ceuta no right to remain in Spain. But Spanish intelligence believes that people smugglers did exploit a distorted interpretation of the ruling.
Subscribe now

## Morocco let it happen
There is very strong evidence that the Moroccan state played a decisive role in this crisis.
Back in May 2021, 8,000 Moroccan migrants entered Ceuta over two days. On that occasion, Morocco had been antagonised by Spain admitting the leader of a pro-independence Western Saharan movement for medical treatment.
Western Sahara is under Moroccan occupation, and there is a powerful movement for independence. As the think tank Chatham House outline:

> “Within months, Spain had abandoned its historic position on Western Sahara – supporting an independence referendum – and instead endorsed Morocco’s autonomy plan for the territory. The lesson for Rabat, perhaps, was that pressure on Spain’s enclaves works.”
This time, the supposed pretext may have been Sánchez’s visit to Morocco’s regional rival, Algeria. He was attempting to repair relations that Algeria had severed after Spain shifted towards Morocco’s position on Western Sahara. Sánchez also discussed increasing the gas supply through a pipeline that bypasses Morocco and runs directly from Algeria to Spain.
But this was an extraordinarily weak pretext for enabling such a vast movement of people and endangering so many lives. The meeting had been announced in advance, and it did not reverse Spain’s highly favourable position towards Morocco on Western Sahara.
An Associated Press photographer at the scene said Moroccan gendarmes made no attempt to intervene as thousands of people moved past their positions towards Ceuta.
El País reported the same pattern. Moroccan auxiliary forces managed the movement of the crowd while police and gendarmes stood guard. This non-intervention continued from approximately midday on Thursday until Friday morning. The newspaper described the initial inhibition as “patent”.
In other words, Morocco’s authorities maintained order while leaving the route into Ceuta open.
Only after tens of thousands had crossed did the authorities deploy tear gas, water cannon and physical force. That matters. Once Morocco’s security forces decided to stop the movement, they demonstrated that they were perfectly capable of doing so.
More devastatingly, a report published by El Español cites sources in the Guardia Civil’s general staff who claimed Spanish border-surveillance cameras identified members of Morocco’s intelligence service among those who entered Ceuta.
Those sources claim that the alleged operatives took part to supervise the movement, observe Spain’s deployment, and monitor the response of the Spanish security forces. Spain’s intelligence sources are reported to have corroborated the Guardia Civil’s identification. The paper says other such infiltrations had been detected in previous Ceuta and Melilla crises.
Another report suggests that Spanish intelligence was concerned by nearly a thousand people swimming into Ceuta in a 10-day period. They interpreted the growing pressure as a potential test from the Moroccan state.
Spanish government sources told El País that an entry on this scale would not have been possible without the passivity of Morocco’s security forces.
Spain has continued publicly to praise Morocco as an ally. But Madrid has every reason to avoid an open confrontation: it depends on Morocco for migration control, counter-terrorism cooperation and the management of the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla.
Subscribe now

## Morocco’s alliance with Israel and the US
All of this matters because Morocco is a close ally of both Israel and the United States, with deep economic, military, intelligence and security ties to both countries.
Morocco is one of the Arab and African countries closest to the US. It’s a major non-NATO ally which buys vast quantities of US weapons and host of African Lion, AFRICOM’s largest annual military exercise. Its security services have a strong relationship with US intelligence and law enforcement. It has a free trade agreement which underpins annual goods trade worth $7.4 billion a year.
In 2020, Morocco normalised diplomatic relations with Israel. Israel gained security access and influence in North Africa, while Morocco acquired Israeli weapons and defence technology, along with expanded intelligence and cybersecurity cooperation.
In November 2021, Israel and Morocco signed a defence memorandum establishing a formal framework for intelligence cooperation, military exercises, defence-industrial collaboration, Israeli arms sales and exchanges between the two countries’ security apparatuses.
At a meeting in January, Morocco and Israel signed a joint military work plan for 2026.
None of that proves that Israel or the US was involved in the Ceuta crisis. But it establishes the context in which the crisis took place – and the states with which Morocco’s security establishment is most closely aligned.
Subscribe now

## The US connection
Donald Trump has been enraged by Spain’s opposition to the illegal war on Iran and to Israel’s genocide in Gaza. He recently demanded an end to trade with Spain, calling the country “terrible”.
In February, written testimony from a senior fellow at the neoconservative Hudson Institute to a House Foreign Affairs subcommittee stated:

> “Morocco has been using migrants to change Spanish policy, and it has succeeded.”
In March, the right-wing, pro-war commentator and former Pentagon official Michael Rubin openly called on Morocco to organise a mass civilian mobilisation against Ceuta and Melilla.
He proposed that Moroccans gather at the frontier, send bulldozers forward and enter the cities unarmed in order to raise the Moroccan flag. Rubin is a prominent figure in Washington’s pro-Israel and national-security world.
In the weeks that followed, the House Appropriations Committee published its report on the 2027 State Department funding bill. It did two striking things.
First, it directed at least $20 million in National Security Investment Programmes and another $20 million in Foreign Military Financing to Morocco.
Second, it stated that the “Spanish-administered cities of Ceuta and Melilla are located in Moroccan territory”, noted Morocco’s claim to the cities and supported State Department efforts to encourage talks over their “future status”.
The House passed the accompanying bill on 15 July by 217 votes to 209 – just 15 days before the mass crossing.
Two days before the crossing, the US Trade and Development Agency agreed to fund a $5.7 million early engineering study for an ammonia project in Moroccan-controlled Western Sahara. It was the first US government financing for a private-sector project there.
At the signing ceremony, the US ambassador declared:

> “America is in the Moroccan Sahara.”
Trump’s recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara was no longer merely diplomatic. Washington was now attaching concrete rewards to it.
The US first recognised Morocco’s claim over Western Sahara in 2020, in exchange for Morocco normalising relations with Israel. The Trump administration subsequently announced initiatives intended to mobilise $5 billion in investment involving Morocco and the wider region, as well as a weapons package.
That has now increased to at least $40 million for Moroccan security and investment programmes.
Again, none of this proves that the US organised the Ceuta crossings. But the sequence is striking: growing US hostility towards Spain, open encouragement for Morocco to mobilise against the Spanish enclaves, congressional language backing Morocco’s territorial claim, increased military support and the first US financing of a private project in Moroccan-controlled Western Sahara.
Subscribe now

## The Israeli connection
Prominent Israeli figures were certainly jubilant about the crisis.
Danny Danon, Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations, declared:

> “Spain, which never misses an opportunity to lecture Israel, has declared a state of emergency in Ceuta following the crisis over its immigration policy.”
Spain had not, in fact, declared any state of emergency.
Meanwhile, the far-right Israeli minister Itamar Ben-Gvir demanded that Sánchez “open the doors of Spain and grant refuge to the residents of Gaza who seek to emigrate”.
But the most important evidence concerns the online campaign that helped bring tens of thousands of people to the border.
Anonymous social-media accounts circulated a specific message: that the Spanish border was open and that people could enter without documents.
El País found that the anonymous campaign did more than claim the frontier was open. It distributed practical advice intended to help people reach and cross the border, while one of the communities promoting the journey attracted more than 20,000 followers before being closed. The original organisers have proved difficult to trace, and automated accounts may have helped spread their material.
According to El País, the original accounts largely vanished, automated amplification may have been involved and the initial trigger has still not been identified.
After the crisis exploded, the Spanish fact-checking organisation Maldita documented the rapid appearance of posts using the hashtags #FreeCeuta and #FreeMelilla from Israeli and pro-Israeli accounts.
Al Jazeera’s open-source unit conducted a broader analysis. It found dozens of known and anonymous Israel-linked or Israel-supporting accounts using almost identical framing. The same maps, phrases and hashtags appeared repeatedly.
They found that AI-generated scenes were used to exaggerate the disorder in Ceuta. Posts described the crisis as Spain’s punishment for supporting Palestine. Hananya Naftali, a former digital-media official associated with Benjamin Netanyahu, participated in the campaign.
The timing and wording were so closely aligned that the investigators regarded them as strongly suggestive of central coordination.
That does not prove that Israel was behind the original accounts. But it would be extraordinarily naive to pretend that Israel lacks either the means or the record to conduct precisely this sort of operation.
Subscribe now

## Israel has form
France’s agency for combating foreign digital interference has accused the Israeli company BlackCore of targeting elections in several countries.
These included Scotland, where hundreds of coordinated accounts bombarded John Swinney, the SNP and the Scottish government after their criticism of Israel’s assault on Gaza. Before effectively disappearing from public view after Reuters approached it, BlackCore had publicly promoted its ability to conduct sophisticated influence operations for governments and political campaigns.
Then there is Black Cube, founded by former Israeli intelligence officers and known as the “private Mossad”. It has been accused of using fake identities, bogus job offers, hidden cameras and manufactured corruption allegations against journalists, activists and pro-Palestinian politicians – including in an alleged attempt to destabilise Slovenia’s government immediately before an election.
One of Black Cube’s advisers is Giora Eiland, the former head of Israel’s national security council. Eiland has publicly advocated depriving Gaza’s population of food, water and fuel, and welcomed the spread of epidemics as a means of securing Israeli victory.
In 2023, an undercover investigation exposed another Israeli operation, Team Jorge. The group’s founder boasted to undercover reporters that his organisation had covertly intervened in dozens of elections around the world. Its technology allowed operatives to manufacture and manage elaborate digital identities across numerous platforms, complete with some of the financial and commercial accounts that would make them appear authentic.
Its software controlled thousands of fake online personas, some equipped with email accounts, credit cards, cryptocurrency wallets and carefully fabricated lives.
We also know that Israel’s government financed a covert campaign using fake social-media accounts to target American politicians with pro-Israel propaganda. Israeli Pegasus spyware has been deployed against politicians and dissidents around the world. Israel has also dramatically expanded its official propaganda budget.
So let us be precise. None of this establishes who started the Ceuta campaign.
But the techniques used there – anonymous accounts, detailed operational instructions, automated amplification and the rapid disappearance of the original network – bear an obvious resemblance to methods repeatedly used by Israeli firms and state-backed operations elsewhere.
The question is not whether Israel possesses the machinery to manipulate foreign politics in this way. It unquestionably does.
The question is whether that machinery was deployed here.
Subscribe now

## A plan to help Morocco “reclaim its north”
There is another striking piece of context.
In April 2026, the Israeli news outlet Ynet published an article headlined: “Abraham Accords reach the Strait: how Israel can help Morocco reclaim its north.”
It was written by a Morocco-based analyst affiliated with the hard-right US-based Middle East Forum, which has previously supported the far-right British figure Tommy Robinson.
The article described developments in Washington as the “architecture of a coordinated strategic repositioning”. It argued that Israel was uniquely placed to help Morocco exploit Spain’s deteriorating relationships with Washington and Jerusalem.
The author proposed three roles for Israel:

- direct diplomatic signalling in support of Morocco’s position;

- lobbying and amplification within Washington;

- repeated attacks on Spain as hypocritical for criticising Israeli territorial policy while retaining Ceuta and Melilla.
He concluded that Israeli support for Morocco’s claim would both impose a political cost on Spain and strengthen a partner with a strategically important position on the Strait of Gibraltar.
Israel has also adopted a strategy of promoting the European far right and its anti-migrant narratives. That includes Vox - the Spanish far-right party which has a militant pro-Israel orientation, and which has links with Netanyahu’s Likud party.
In an interview on Fox News’ Hang Out with Sean Hannity, Netanyahu cited someone who had supposedly been asked:

> “Why are you studying Arabic?”
The answer:

> “Because I want to be able to go to London and Paris.”
Netanyahu continued:

> “If you lose control over your borders, you lose control over your fate and your destiny and your future.”
To be clear, just 0.8 per cent of Londoners use Arabic as their main language, while Arab people make up around 1.6 per cent of the city’s population.
This was Netanyahu scaremongering about a supposed Arab invasion of Europe – the same narrative being used to exploit the Ceuta crisis.
Subscribe now

## Spanish suspicions
Spanish politicians have themselves voiced suspicions about what happened.
After Danny Danon attacked Spain over Ceuta, the Spanish Transport Minister Óscar Puente responded:

> “Well, things are starting to get pretty clear.”
The implication was obvious: Puente was hinting at Israeli involvement.
Gabriel Rufián, a left-wing Spanish politician, posted:

> “The Moroccan dictatorship, in the service of the US and Israel, is once again blackmailing Spain and Europe this summer by turning its own people into disposable cannon fodder.
“Something that, instead of being the subject of partisan politicking, should be the subject of a cross-cutting State pact.”
Spanish experts have raised similar questions.
Pedro Rodríguez, a professor of international relations, said that the crisis occurred because “Morocco wanted it to happen”. He described it as a display of strategic realignment in which Morocco was aligning itself with the United States and Israel while demonstrating Spain’s inability to control its own territory.
And Kenneth Roth - former executive director of Human Rights Watch - posted:

> “Why would Israel want its ally Morocco to control Ceuta as opposed to its critic Spain? One reason may be that Ceuta is the closest point in Africa to Europe, sitting astride the Strait of Gibraltar, meaning that Spain currently controls both sides of the strait. The Strait of Gibraltar is only 8 miles across, as opposed to the Strait of Hormuz, which is 21 miles. If Iran can control the Strait of Hormuz, Spain could easily control the Strait of Gibraltar and potentially block Israeli access to the Atlantic.”
Subscribe now

## What can we conclude?
None of this proves for certain that Israel or the US helped orchestrate the crisis. That caveat matters.
But it would be equally unserious to dismiss the possibility out of hand.
Morocco is a close US and Israeli ally, with deep security and intelligence ties to both states. It has previously facilitated mass crossings into Ceuta to extract political concessions from Spain. On this occasion, its security forces were visibly passive until tens of thousands of people had crossed – and then demonstrated that they were entirely capable of stopping the movement.
Washington had just increased military and economic support for Morocco, financed a project in Moroccan-controlled Western Sahara and endorsed language treating Ceuta and Melilla as territories whose future status should be negotiated.
Senior US and Israeli figures immediately seized on the crisis to attack Spain and promote the idea of an Arab “invasion” of Europe.
Anonymous social-media accounts of unknown origin played a crucial role in mobilising people, providing practical instructions and spreading the claim that the border was open. Many of those accounts then vanished. Israel has an extensive record of state-backed and private influence operations using precisely these methods.
That does not prove the case.
At the very least, Israel, the US and the far-right in general have shamelessly exploited this crisis.
Whether that involvement goes deeper surely demands investigation.
Help us take on the Establishment media by becoming a free or paid subscriber.
